data_quality_warning: AoFrio is a distressed NZX micro-cap: 15 years of statutory losses, reported FCF negative in seven of the last eight years, an on-demand NZ$10m trade finance facility, and a mid-2026 capital raise that brought in NZ$8.9m of a NZ$15m target. The base and bear scenarios produce no equity value from projected cash flows; only the bull scenario does. Read the output as a cash-flow floor check, not a precise fair value: the market price is option value on the SCS 800 / AoFrio iQ ramp that a DCF on realised financials does not capture.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report, statement of movements in equity ('Share option compensation expensed' NZ$16k); no equity-award tax withholding disclosed. 1H26 charge was nil. SBC has been 0.02-0.13% of revenue since FY2021 and is modelled at 0% (the prior build used 0.1%, worth under NZ$0.001 per share); the row is kept explicit and the house/street band collapses.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-19T03:32:40Z (NZX regular session, Yahoo regularMarketTime; thinly traded, at the 52-week low)
inputs.share_count_basis: 562,618,821 ordinary shares on issue at 30 June 2026 (1H26 interim report note 4.3: 434,232,042 opening + 128,386,779 issued in the May placement and June rights issue). The 4.31m CEO options (exercise price 11.5c, vested 1 Oct 2025) are far out of the money and excluded. Held FLAT: negative projected owner FCF is already deducted from enterprise value, so also diluting the count for the raises that would fund that burn charges it twice. The prior build's funding-dilution mechanism (base +27m, bear +205m shares) is removed for that reason.
inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY0 is the FY2026 estimate, unchanged from the prior build: 1H26 actual 33.8 (Motors 10.6, IoT 23.2) plus a 2H26 estimate of Motors flat at the post-customer-loss run-rate and IoT +5% on 2H25 = 71.1, -14.5% on FY2025's 83.186. Consistent with the August 2026 outlook that a full-year revenue improvement 'now appears unlikely'. Year 1 of every path is FY2027.
inputs.fy2026_stub_note: Because FY0 is FY2026 and the balance sheet is 30 June 2026, the 2H26 cash flow falls between the anchor and the first projected year. It is carried as an equity_bridge item (see there) rather than ignored.
inputs.wacc_rationale: NZD flows, NZD rate: risk-free 4.5% (NZ 10-year government bond, as used in the prior build) + 5.5% ERP x 1.5 beta = 12.75% CAPM cost of equity, + 3.0% micro-cap + 2.5% illiquidity = 18.25%, applied as 18% in ALL scenarios. The prior build also stacked 2.0% customer-concentration and 2.0% funding-risk premia and used 18/20/23% by scenario. Those two premia and the per-scenario spread are removed: the customer loss is already in the FY2026 revenue base, funding stress is already in the bear flows and its 30% weight, and charging them again in the rate prices the same risk twice. With net debt small relative to the risk premia, WACC is taken as the cost of equity. Note the 15% hurdle sits BELOW this 18% discount rate, so hurdle entry prices come out above intrinsic value; for this ticker the intrinsic value is the binding number, not the entry price.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Reported EBITDA is post-IFRS 16, so lease cash (principal NZ$0.302m + interest NZ$0.366m in FY2025; NZ$0.181m + NZ$0.180m in 1H26) is charged through lease_cost_pct_path, and the NZ$4.231m of right-of-use liabilities at 30 June 2026 is excluded from net debt. The D&A path (about NZ$3.3m in year 1) matches FY2025 D&A excluding right-of-use depreciation (3.621 - 0.459 = 3.162). The prior build charged leases in neither the flows nor net debt.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF with the non-US adaptations. AoFrio (formerly Wellington Drive Technologies) is an operating company: it designs EC fan motors and IoT refrigeration controllers (SCS Connect, SCS 800) with an attached SaaS platform (AoFrio iQ) for the cold-drink-equipment and food-retail industries, manufactured under contract in Vietnam. It is not a forestry, rural-land or property vehicle, so no AFFO/NAV route applies. Same model family as the prior (2026-08-08) valuation, which was a hand-built legacy JSON; this is its first build through the Drivers engine. SBC is negligible and the company does not repurchase shares, so the house and street bases effectively coincide. FY2025 lease principal of NZ$0.302m sits in financing and is not in reported_fcf. No interest-income strip: the company carries net debt. Not checked: any NZX trading update released after the 5 August 2026 interim report (none is in the extracted filings).
inputs.precision_note: The engine rounds per-share values to two decimals and money to NZ$0.1m, which is coarse for a share priced under five cents, and it does not floor negative scenario equity at zero. The limited_liability_floor block carries four-decimal per-share values, each derived as valuation.<scenario>.equity_value / shares_outstanding, on both the raw and the floored basis.

equity_bridge.item: 2H26 expected unlevered owner cash flow (stub between the 30 June 2026 balance sheet and FY2027)
equity_bridge.note: FY2026 EBITDA guided 'broadly consistent with 2025' (3.5) less 1H26 actual 0.879 = about 2.6; less 2H26 capex about 4.6 at the 1H26 run-rate (4.604, capital deployment starting 2H26); less lease cash 0.36 and tax 0.05; working capital assumed neutral. An estimate, to be replaced by the FY2026 balance sheet when published.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Historical CAGRs (FY2025 annual basis) are not usable growth anchors. EPS and owner FCF are negative at one or both ends of every window, so no CAGR is computable. Equity shrank 12.6%/yr over three years as losses eroded capital (before the 2026 raise lifted it to 22.955 at 30 June 2026). The 5-year revenue CAGR of 17.7% is a FY2020 COVID-trough base effect and FY2026 revenue is tracking -14.5%. Revenue is therefore built bottom-up from the 1H26 Motors/IoT split.
historical_growth.notes: Reported FCF was negative in FY2018, FY2019, FY2020, FY2022, FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025; only FY2021 (+1.7) was positive. FY2025 FCF of -5.259 reflects capex of 9.078 (10.9% of revenue, 7.978 of it capitalised development) against operating cash flow of 3.819. 1H26 FCF was -5.465. SBC is under 0.15% of revenue in every year, so the owner-FCF and reported-FCF series are effectively the same.

base.lease_cost_pct_path_note: Lease cash of about NZ$0.75m a year, roughly fixed, so it falls as a share of growing revenue.
base.narrative: IoT (SCS Connect, SCS 800, AoFrio iQ) gradually offsets the structurally smaller Motors book; capitalised development keeps capex elevated before moderating; EBITDA margin climbs from 2.5% to 9.8% by year 10, below management's self-funded FY30 target of 10% on NZ$140m.

bull.narrative: The 33 SCS 800 / AoFrio iQ trials convert to purchase orders from 2H26, Food Retail scales beyond its first Latin American supermarket order, and recurring SaaS mix rises; EBITDA margin reaches 16% by year 10, still short of the aspirational FY30 plan.

bear.narrative: Trials do not convert, Motors keeps losing share to lower-specification product with no replacement for the lost US customer, and SaaS revenue stays marginal; owner FCF is negative in every year of the horizon.

scenario_narratives.base: IoT hardware and services grow steadily while Motors stabilises at roughly half its FY2025 size after the largest US customer moved to local sourcing on tariffs. Revenue grows 8-9% a year from the FY2026 base of about NZ$71m, reaching roughly NZ$137m by FY2036 (management's self-funded plan gets to NZ$140m by FY30, six years sooner). Gross margin keeps improving on mix (34.9% in 1H26 against 29.6%), lifting EBITDA margin to just under 10%, but capitalised platform development keeps owner FCF negative until around year 5. Growth, margin, capex, tax and working-capital paths are unchanged from the 2026-08-08 build.
scenario_narratives.bull: The SCS 800 cellular controller and AoFrio iQ, both commercially released in June 2026, convert the 33 customer trials into volume orders; Food Retail becomes a second vertical; deferred revenue (NZ$18.6m at 30 June 2026) and software at a targeted 70% gross margin lift group EBITDA margin to 16%. Owner FCF turns positive by year 3. This is the only scenario with positive equity value, and it needs commercial execution not yet visible in bookings. Driver paths unchanged from the prior build.
scenario_narratives.bear: Purchase orders from the trials do not arrive at scale, remaining motor customers continue shifting to lower-cost specifications, and the business stays a sub-NZ$85m, low-single-digit-margin hardware supplier that capitalises more development than it earns. Owner FCF never turns positive, the terminal value sits on the zero floor, and equity is worth nothing on cash flows: in this path the company depends on repeated raises or a sale, with the on-demand bank facility and its EBITDA/interest covenant as the pressure point. Driver paths unchanged from the prior build.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Unchanged from the prior build. Bear 30%, above the 15% house default, for the realised loss of the largest motor customer, the undersubscribed raise and a repayable-on-demand facility. Base 50% as the most likely path, a slower version of management's self-funded plan. Bull 20%, below the 35% default, because it needs the unproven SCS 800 / AoFrio iQ ramp, a second vertical and margin expansion all to work.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Fundamentals-only floor valuation. A component-built owner-FCF DCF on AoFrio's realised financials gives no equity value in the base and bear scenarios and a positive value only in the bull scenario, so the probability-weighted value is essentially 20% of the bull case. That does not mean the shares are worthless: the market is paying for option value on the IoT/SaaS ramp (a multi-million connected installed base, NZ$18.6m of deferred revenue, 33 SCS 800 / AoFrio iQ trials) and for takeout optionality, none of which a cash-flow DCF captures. An investment here is a venture-style bet on the SaaS conversion, not a value case supported by current cash generation.
valuation_philosophy.unchanged_from_prior: Deliberately left as they were in the 2026-08-08 build, because no filing after the 5 August 2026 interim report is available: the FY2026 revenue base (71.1), every growth, EBITDA-margin, SBC, D&A, capex, cash-tax and working-capital path, terminal growth and cap multiples, the 30/50/20 weights and the 15% hurdle. What would move them: the FY2026 result (due about February 2027) for the revenue base and year-1 margin; evidence of SCS 800 purchase orders in a trading update for the bull weight and early growth years; capex running at the 1H26 rate (12.9% of annualised revenue against 9.5% modelled for FY2027) for the capex path; a covenant breach or further raise for the bear weight.
key_risks_to_valuation: The weighted value rests entirely on the bull scenario; a few points of bull probability or EBITDA margin move it by a large percentage.
The 2H26 cash-flow stub (-2.4) is an estimate; actual working-capital swings in a business with NZ$16m of receivables and NZ$18m of payables can exceed it.
The NZ$10m trade finance facility is repayable on demand and carries an EBITDA/interest covenant that 1H26 EBITDA of 0.9 met only with a 1.2 R&D tax incentive credit.
Capex is mostly capitalised development; if it stays at the 1H26 run-rate the base case burns materially more than modelled.
At an 18% discount rate the hurdle entry price exceeds intrinsic value and is not a usable buy-below signal for this ticker.

limited_liability_floor.note: Shareholders cannot lose more than their investment, so a scenario's equity value cannot be below zero. The engine's intrinsic_value and weighted_iv are raw (unfloored) and negative in base and bear; the floored basis below is the one comparable with the prior build's 0.0092 headline. Both scenarios with negative equity (base, bear) are findings: projected cash flows do not cover net debt and the 2H26 burn on those paths.
